patient_information: A 6-year-old boy from Malawi, known to be HIV-positive but not yet on antiretroviral therapy (ART).
chief_complaint: High fever, dyspnoea, dry cough, and impaired consciousness.
history_of_present_illness: Symptoms of high fever, dyspnoea, and a dry cough started 3 days prior to admission; presumptive antimalarial treatment was initiated upon admission with malaria smear results pending.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Patient is from Malawi; measles is a highly contagious viral infection transmitted through droplets, and large outbreaks occur worldwide, with higher case fatality rates in developing countries and children under 5 years.
vitals:
Temperature: 39.8
C (103.6
F); Blantyre coma score: 3/5.
physical_exam: Laboured breathing, coryza, bilateral conjunctivitis, a fine maculopapular rash behind both ears and on the forehead, and bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy.
labs_and_diagnostics: Initial malaria smear results were pending, but later turned out to be negative.
differential_diagnosis: Malaria, typhoid fever, atypical pneumonia, various viral infections (rubella, enterovirus infection, infectious mononucleosis), and bacterial infections (scarlet fever, meningococcal disease, rickettsial infections); measles was highly suspected given the 'three Cs' (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis) and rash.
management_and_clinical_course: Initially treated with presumptive antimalarial treatment; required IV fluids and vitamin A for corneal protection. Malaria treatment was stopped after negative smears. The rash covered the trunk, and skin scaling started over the chest within 3 days. The boy developed severe pneumonia and received antibiotic treatment. After recovery, antiretroviral therapy (ART) was started in the out-patient-clinic. Patient was isolated due to contagiousness.
